webPolicy.summary: Finish Yes opens a Radio-owned Save dialog only for the session's own committed capture still held by the document; no I/O, picker or host request; disabled with a reason without browser support; web default Cancel.
The dialog keeps the exact committed lease object; Begin and the verified exit require that identity, so a same-id or equal-valued lease is never admitted, claimed, recorded under or released.

Separate finish claim domain bound to the lease object and the claimed data/generation/metadata/samples; recorder refusal order claim, capture-lease, then the shared generic tail; no cross-use with generic claims; the generic recorder still refuses any lease.
Only a live verified receipt for the dialog's lease object, data and generation ends the finish, with exactly one release of the session's own lease; no analysis, erase or arming.
Readiness: own lease held, no analysis read, no output claim; analysis.modal is not a condition (no deadlock). Arming Save and Analysis Save/Download stay refused under the lease.
Back (Escape) returns to the question with the lease held; refused while an attempt holds the output claim; No/Cancel unchanged and refused while the dialog is open.
Choose is its own click, synchronous up to showSaveFilePicker; detail > 1 ignored; a synchronous picker failure releases the claim at once.
Attempt tokens and liveness; route hide, project operation or unmount make the attempt dead for good; output claim released only after cleanup; the capture lease stays held.
The arming and finish Radio Saves never coexist; one running attempt and one shared output claim.
Focus: Back on entry, Cancel at the question after Back, Record after the verified exit; held keys ignored; wrapping layout at 1440/375/320.

limits: Static disassembly is not CLEA execution, a native exception oracle, x87/GDI/code-page/OS equivalence or physical write durability.
The web ends the finish only on a verified receipt; natively a normal return (including a cancelled dialog) ends it, and the exception continuation is unknown.
A hung provider keeps the dialog, the output claim, the capture lease and Analysis Load blocked until it settles; no timeout or forced release.
The unmount teardown has no runtime witness (the App never unmounts the workspace); only the pure late-callback/lease-identity rule is tested.
No en.json key is added; radioReceiver.record.yesGated is left unchanged and is no longer read by the finish question.
No original binary bytes or research dumps are copied into the product.
